name: ULN2003ADR
title: ULN2002A, ULN2003A, ULN2003AI, ULN2004A, ULQ2003A, ULQ2004A: seven-channel 50 V, 500 mA Darlington arrays
summary: Seven NPN Darlington pairs with open collectors rated 50 V and 500 mA each, a shared emitter pin and a clamp diode on every output to a common COM pin for relays and other inductive loads. The input network sets the logic family: ULN2002A for 14 V to 25 V PMOS, the 2003 types (2.7 kΩ) for TTL and 5 V CMOS, the 2004 types (10.5 kΩ) for 6 V to 15 V CMOS. ULN, ULN...I and ULQ grades cover -20 to 70 °C, -40 to 105 °C and -40 to 85 °C. ULN2003ADR is the ULN2003A in SOIC-16 on a 2500-piece reel.

circuits.title: P-MOS output driving an inductive load (ULN2002A)
circuits.description: A p-channel MOS output, its source on the VSS rail, drives input 7B of a ULN2002A directly. Output 7C sinks the current of an inductive load whose other end is on the load supply V; COM is also on V so the internal clamp diode catches the turn-off spike. E is grounded and the other six channels are unused.

circuits.title: TTL output driving lamps (ULN2003A, ULQ2003A)
circuits.description: A TTL totem-pole output (Q1 to Q3, R1 to R3, D1) drives input 7B of a ULN2003A or ULQ2003A. Seven lamps run from the supply V, one on each output 1C to 7C. COM goes to ground through a switch marked Lamp Test; with the switch closed every lamp draws current to ground through its clamp diode. E is grounded; inputs 1B to 6B are unconnected.

circuits.title: CMOS output with an external PNP for a heavier load (ULN2004A, ULQ2004A)
circuits.description: A CMOS inverter output on VDD drives input 7B of a ULN2004A or ULQ2004A. Output 7C pulls the base of an external PNP transistor low through R1, with R2 from base to emitter; the PNP emitter is on the supply V and its collector feeds an inductive load to ground, with D1 across the load as a flyback diode. COM is tied to V and E to ground; the other channels are unused.

circuits.title: TTL output with a pull-up resistor for more input drive (ULN2003A, ULQ2003A)
circuits.description: A TTL totem-pole output drives input 7B of a ULN2003A or ULQ2003A, with RP from VCC to the input raising the current the input receives when the gate output is high. Output 7C sinks an inductive load from the supply V, COM is tied to V for clamping, and E is grounded; the other channels are unused.

where.θJA: junction-to-ambient thermal impedance: D 73, N 67, NS 64, PW 108 °C/W

where.II: input current, held fixed for VCE(sat) and varied for hFE

operation.text: Seven NPN Darlington pairs share one emitter pin, E (pin 8). Each pair's collector is an open output rated 50 V and 500 mA, and each output has a clamp diode whose cathode goes to the shared COM pin (pin 9) for inductive loads. Pairs may be connected in parallel to carry more current.

Inside each pair the first transistor's base has 7.2 kΩ to the output transistor's base, and the output transistor's base has 3 kΩ to E; a diode joins E (anode) to the input (cathode). ULN2002A puts a 7 V zener and 10.5 kΩ in series with the input, for 14 V to 25 V PMOS drive. ULN2003A, ULN2003AI and ULQ2003A use a 2.7 kΩ base resistor, for TTL or 5 V CMOS. ULN2004A and ULQ2004A use 10.5 kΩ, for CMOS on 6 V to 15 V; they need less input current than the 2003 types and less input voltage than ULN2002A. All resistor values are nominal.
The diode between E and each collector is a parasitic structure and is not for conducting current. A collector that is driven below ground needs an external Schottky diode to clamp the undershoot.

The allowed peak collector current per output falls as duty cycle and the number of outputs on at the same time rise. Figure 14 gives this for the D package at 70 °C and Figure 15 for the N package at 85 °C.

Delays are measured between the 50 % points of input and output. VOH after switching is measured with a 2 mH and 200 Ω load to VS, a 1N3064 diode from output to VS, COM open, 15 pF load capacitance, and a 40 µs input pulse from a 50 Ω generator at 12.5 kHz.
SN75468 and SN75469 are 100 V versions that can replace ULN2003A and ULN2004A respectively. ULQ2003A-Q1 and ULQ2004A-Q1 are automotive-qualified versions of the ULQ types.
Named uses: driving relays, hammers, lamps, LED and gas-discharge displays and lines, and buffering logic.
